tagline.text: A little Venice in Manila, gondolas included

location.label: Location
location.text: McKinley Hill, Taguig, Metro Manila (Fort Bonifacio)

best_season.label: Best time to visit
best_season.text: Year-round (dry-season evenings from November to February are the most pleasant)

budget.label: Budget
budget.text: About ₱800–2,500 per person (including gondola, meal and transport)

children.text: An open-air shopping mall in McKinley Hill, Taguig, modeled on Venice, Italy. Ride a gondola rowed by a gondolier along the 200m man-made canal, then have dinner at a canal-side restaurant with views of the Rialto Bridge and bell tower replicas. Close to BGC and the airport, it makes an easy half-day outing.
Venice Grand Canal Mall is a shopping mall in McKinley Hill, Taguig, Metro Manila, built by property developer Megaworld and modeled on the Grand Canal of Venice, Italy. It opened on
September 18, 2015
and was designed in consultation with Rome-based architect Paolo Marioni. A man-made canal about
long and about
wide runs through the middle of the mall, lined on both sides with pastel buildings, arcades and balconies, which has earned it the nickname of the "most romantic mall" in the Philippines. In
it won the top prize for retail architectural design at the Philippines Property Awards.

The star here is the canal, not the shopping. Gondolas rowed by gondoliers in striped shirts and straw hats set off from the dock under the Rialto Bridge replica and circle the canal, and swan-shaped pedal boats float on the water too. Even at a slow stroll you can see everything in
15–20 minutes

, from the Ponte de Amore, the bridge of love where couples hang padlocks, to the tower modeled on St Mark's Campanile and Venice Piazza with its lawn. Admission is free, and the only things that cost money are the gondola and your meal.

It is not a big mall. With three levels of shops, restaurants, a cinema and a supermarket, it is closer to a neighborhood mall, and you may be disappointed if you come expecting the shopping of a mega mall. What it does offer is an atmosphere that is hard to find at other malls in Manila: pasta, wine and coffee at an outdoor table overlooking the canal. It is at its most beautiful at dusk, when the string lights above the canal come on and the building lights are reflected in the water.
McKinley Hill, where the mall stands, is a Megaworld township of about 50 hectares styled after southern Europe, right next to the southern edge of
Bonifacio Global City

. The Embassy of the Republic of Korea is on the same Upper McKinley Road, so Korean residents coming for consular business can easily drop by, and it is not far from Ninoy Aquino International Airport (NAIA), which makes it a good half-day stop on the day you arrive or leave. It suits couples on a date, families with children and travelers who love taking photos.

blocks.title: Ride a gondola around the canal

children.text: Board a gondola at the dock under the Rialto Bridge replica. The fare is reported to be about
per person on a boat shared with other guests, or about
to hire a whole boat, and each boat takes up to 6 people. The gondolier may even sing for you.

blocks.title: Rialto Bridge and the bridge of love

children.text: The white arched bridge across the canal is the Rialto Bridge replica, and from the top you can fit the canal and the pastel buildings into one shot. On the heart-decorated Ponte de Amore, couples hang padlocks with their names on them. Padlocks are sold on site.

blocks.title: Venice Piazza and the bell tower

children.text: This square is modeled on Piazza San Marco, with a tower resembling the Venetian campanile and a yellow clock tower building around a lawn. Pigeon feeding takes place in the late afternoon, and a small train for children runs here too.
If the gondola line is long or you are with children, try a swan boat that you pedal yourself. The fare is reported to be about
; check at the dock ticket booth whether the boats are running and what they cost.

Outdoor tables of Italian restaurants and cafes line the canal. An evening of pasta, pizza and wine while gondolas glide past is the greatest pleasure of this mall. Canal-side seats fill up early at dinner time.
Around sunset, about
, the string lights, street lamps and building lights come on one after another. With the lights reflected in the water and the gondolas in the same frame, this is the best time for photos.

On the third level, on the Campus Avenue side, there is a Catholic chapel decorated with Gothic-style arches and statues of angels. It is a quiet place to pray even inside a shopping mall; check the notice at the entrance for Mass times.

Head into the indoor mall to escape the heat or rain. The stained-glass dome ceiling of the central hall and the Venetian-style balcony decor are worth a look, and Venice Cineplex has theaters with reclining seats.
Arrive at the mall by Grab. Choose the main drop-off of "Venice Grand Canal Mall" as your drop-off point
Walk through the indoor mall out to the canal and buy your gondola ticket first. On weekends, get your place in the queue right away
Walk a full loop along the canal and take photos at the Rialto Bridge and the bridge of love
When your turn comes, ride the gondola once around the canal
Go to Venice Piazza to see the bell tower and clock tower and watch the pigeon feeding
Watch the canal light up from the top of the Rialto Bridge or the second-level balcony walkway
Have dinner at a canal-side restaurant
Take night photos and head back to your accommodation by Grab
On weekend and holiday evenings, the wait for a gondola can exceed
1 hour
. On such days, buy your ticket as soon as you arrive and finish your stroll and photos while you wait to save time.

The three places are
5–20 minutes
apart by car, so they are easy to combine in one day. For the cemetery's opening hours and visitor etiquette, see the
Manila American Cemetery
entry.
The mall is about
6–9km
from Ninoy Aquino International Airport. By Grab it takes
20–30 minutes
without traffic and more than
50 minutes
at rush hour, and the fare is about
There is no convenient direct public transport from the airport to the mall, so Grab or a taxi is the most practical choice. Enter "Venice Grand Canal Mall" as your destination.
From BGC High Street it takes about
10–20 minutes
and costs about
. From Ayala Center in Makati it takes about
20–40 minutes
and costs about
When heading back, book from the main drop-off or the entrance on the Upper McKinley Road side. Cars are hard to get on Friday evenings and rainy days, so book before you finish your meal.
City bus route 18, which links North EDSA and PITX, runs via C-5 Road and Upper McKinley Road and stops at the bus stop in front of the mall. If you board around Market! Market!, the fare is about
Route 4 from PITX via Buendia also has Venice Mall as its terminus, but many buses end their run at Kalayaan. Before boarding, ask the conductor whether the bus goes all the way to McKinley Hill.
The BGC Bus, which links Ayala and BGC, does not come into McKinley Hill. Take the BGC Bus to Market! Market!, then transfer to bus 18 or a Grab.
From Guadalupe station on MRT Line 3, take a jeepney bound for AFP/PNP Housing and get off at Lawton Avenue, from where it is a walk of about
to the mall. The jeepney base fare is about
The transfer is complicated and the walk has little shade, so this is not recommended for first-time visitors. Booking a Grab from the station is easier.
Everything inside the mall is on foot. It is about
3–5 minutes
from the main drop-off to the canal and about
5 minutes
from the canal to Venice Piazza.
McKinley Town Center, where the Korean Embassy is located, is about
1km
along Upper McKinley Road toward C-5 Road, roughly
15 minutes
on foot.
There is basement parking, but it fills up early on weekend evenings. Check the official Megaworld Lifestyle Malls information for parking rates.
The canal and the dining strip are mostly outdoors, so the weather matters a lot. The best time is the evening in
November–February
, the breezy, cooler part of the dry season. In
March–May
daytime temperatures climb to around
, which makes a midday walk along the canal hard going, so it is better to go after
In the rainy season of
June–October
afternoon showers are frequent, and typhoons sometimes pass through in
July–October
. The gondolas and swan boats stop in heavy rain and lightning, so plan around the indoor mall and cinema at such times. Christmas decorations and lights go up from
September
, and in
December
events such as a Christmas parade are sometimes held, so there is more to see but also bigger crowds. During the week of Valentine's Day in
February
, evening waits also get longer with couples.

children.text: Prices are approximate as of
and may vary depending on local conditions.
There is no need to stay in McKinley Hill just to see the mall. Most visitors stay in BGC or Makati and come by Grab; international chain hotels in BGC cost about
a night and serviced residences about
. There are also many condo rentals within McKinley Hill, which suit those looking for a quiet base for embassy business or an early flight.

Italian food takes center stage. Toni & Sergio, which has outdoor seating by the canal, the Philippine Italian restaurant chain CIBO, Mama Lou's and Italianni's serve pasta and pizza, while you can have Filipino food at Mesa and Korean-style grilled pork belly at Samgyupsalamat. There are also fast-food outlets such as Jollibee and McDonald's, so it is easy to choose according to your budget. Tenants change often, so if there is a place you want to visit, check the mall's store directory first.
The mall's official hours are
daily. Some restaurants stay open later, and hours are sometimes extended on weekends and in peak season, so if you plan to go late, confirm by calling the main line at (02) 8462-8888.
Arrive at
and you can see the daytime scenery, dusk and the night views in one visit.
Weekday daytime is best if you want to take photos in peace. On weekend and holiday evenings it is so crowded that it is hard even to stand on the bridges.
If you plan to ride a gondola, go to the ticket booth as soon as you arrive. Buying your ticket first and then strolling and eating cuts down the waiting time.

The best photo spots are the top of the Rialto Bridge, the second-level balcony walkway where the canal curves, and in front of the bridge of love. Your phone battery drains fast, so bring a power bank.
There is little shade around the canal. Bring a hat, water and a handheld fan during the day, and take a break in the indoor mall when it gets hot.
Pets are allowed in this mall. Check the rules in advance, such as registering for the Megaworld Lifestyle Malls Pet Pass.
If you are visiting the Korean Embassy for consular business, the mall is a good place to walk over to for lunch afterward. Check the embassy's notices for consular hours and appointments.

The gondolas stop in rain, lightning and strong winds, and the days and hours of operation have also varied over time. At one point they ran only on weekend afternoons, so if the gondola is the reason for your visit, check the mall's latest announcements before you go.
Do not climb over the canal railings or sit children on them. The waterside pavement is slippery when it rains.
The gondola rocks a lot when you get on and off. Move one at a time as the gondolier directs, and pregnant women or those with limited mobility should not push themselves.
Crowds gather on weekend evenings and during the Christmas season. Keep your phone and wallet in a bag worn in front, and do not let go of your child's hand.
At rush hour (
), C-5 Road and Lawton Avenue are heavily congested. If you are going to the airport after dinner, leave
1 hour
earlier than usual.
Gondola and boat fares and opening hours change without notice. Treat the amounts in this guide as a reference only and confirm at the ticket booth on site.
